ai.description: The Desert Monitor reaches 1.3m in length. It is pale yellow to grey with dark crossbands. Key features include a rounded snout and nostrils positioned closer to the eyes than the tip of the snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: Unlike the Bengal Monitor, *Varanus griseus* has nostrils located closer to the eyes than the snout tip and lacks the distinct dark temporal streak behind the eye.
ai.habitat: The desert monitor inhabits arid and semi-arid regions, including sandy deserts and scrublands, typically at low altitudes below 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The desert monitor is a diurnal predator that actively hunts across vast territories, using its keen sense of smell to track prey like rodents, lizards, and eggs.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Varanus griseus* is oviparous, laying a single clutch of 7–20 eggs annually. Breeding occurs during the summer months, typically between May and July.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Varanus griseus* occurs across the arid regions of Northwest India, primarily in Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Punjab, typically inhabiting sandy deserts and scrublands.
